principles: Each DONE predicate has one executable definition consumed by all readiness surfaces.
Keep stable blocker codes, first-failure diagnostics, and read-only evidence inspection.
Use executable consumer tests for behavior and bounded structural checks for the thin shared entry points.
Keep the change limited to DONE/preflight parity and its directly blocking evidence repair.
drivers: Review mutations proved source-semantic inference could falsely accept different inputs, outer guards, and discarded results.
The human approved a shared predicate design after the convergence freeze.
Existing predicates and public behavior already have executable RED/GREEN coverage.

options.name: Shared lazy evaluator in machine.ts
pros: One ordered definition for gate, diagnostics, and oracle
Generic projection carries future failures automatically
cons: Requires a bounded change to the formerly protected DONE branch and careful compatibility tests

options.name: Extend the source-semantic parser
cons: Requires interpreting arbitrary control flow and value provenance
Verified bypasses make this assurance unreliable and repeated expansion unbounded

options.name: Extract a new aggregate module
cons: Requires moving reviewer dependencies or introducing a module cycle
Adds a file and migration surface without improving this bounded proof

rationale: The human-authorized replan replaces the failed parser with a shared ordered evaluator exported by machine.ts. Thin machine consumers preserve early failure behavior; the oracle generically consumes every result. The verifier inventories the shared source reachable from DONE and checks explicit thin adapters, while executable tests establish behavior and mutation rejection.

preMortem.scenario: Aggregation eagerly reads downstream artifacts after an early failure.
preMortem.trigger: Missing test evidence with incomplete legacy artifacts.
preMortem.consequence: Existing safe failures throw or change precedence.
preMortem.mitigation: Use lazy ordered evaluation and test first-failure diagnostics and read calls.

preMortem.scenario: Oracle silently drops a newly added shared predicate.
preMortem.trigger: A new evaluator result has no presentation row.
preMortem.consequence: Preflight misses a real DONE blocker.
preMortem.mitigation: Generic final projection appends missing failures; execute future-predicate mutation against actual consumers.

preMortem.scenario: Adapters change input target or discard failures.
preMortem.trigger: Wrong root/story argument, outer skip, or discarded emitted row.
preMortem.consequence: Consumers see different states or report false readiness.
preMortem.mitigation: Check exact thin adapter shapes and execute mutations with captured reader inputs and final rows.

preMortem.scenario: Refactor changes completion-snapshot or stricter preflight semantics.
preMortem.trigger: Wrapper root, completed snapshot, delivery or review assurance evaluation.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve existing extra preflight rows and test wrapper-root, snapshot and live gate behavior.
